verdict.summary: A tidy tiered timber pavilion on a stone plinth that reads as a generic pagoda or stepped pavilion, not a Japanese tea house: the roof is a stepped lid with no curved eaves, the walls have no white paper screens, and the garden elements are absent.

issues.problem: Hipped-and-gabled roof reads as a stepped ziggurat/lid; stair-stepped tiers, no deep overhang, no curved eaves
issues.fix: Replace the stacked stair tiers with a single hipped roof plane plus a gable, push the eaves out 2-3 blocks, and curve the eave corners with stair/slab steps so the roof edge lifts upward.

issues.problem: Walls are dark timber with open holes; no white sliding paper-screen panels in dark frames
issues.fix: Fill the wall bays between the timber posts with white concrete or white wool panels set inside dark log/stripped-oak frames, and leave one panel set as a sliding track offset.

issues.problem: No stone lantern, maple tree, or stepping stones; the torch posts stand in for the lantern
issues.fix: Add a stone lantern (stone brick base, stone slab, lantern) beside the walk, a stepping-stone path of stone-brick or andesite pads leading to the entry, and a maple tree (oak leaves in red/orange or a mangrove-style canopy) in the corner.

issues.problem: Engawa veranda is only a thin ledge at the base; reads as a step rather than a deck
issues.fix: Widen the veranda to a 2-block wooden deck around the front and sides with a railing of fences or stripped-log posts.

issues.problem: Monochrome dark brown and grey; no contrast to set off the timber
issues.fix: Introduce white screens and pale stone (white or light-gray plinth) so the building separates from the dark brown wood, and use a dark-gray roof tile block to pick up the tile language.
